concepts.title: Standard Form and Checking Roots
concepts.definition: A quadratic equation in standard form is ax squared + bx + c = 0 with a nonzero; a number is a root of the equation if substituting it satisfies the equation - checking this identifies whether given values are solutions.
concepts.key_idea: Substitute to test: a root satisfies the equation; else it is not a root.
question_patterns: check whether the given value is a root of the given quadratic equation
write the given equation in standard form and identify a, b, c
determine whether the given equation is quadratic - justify
represent the given situation as a quadratic equation
verify that x = 2 satisfies the given equation
find the value of k for which x is a root

solution_steps.explain: Bring all terms to one side as ax squared + bx + c = 0.
Replace x by the value and simplify both sides.
Zero on satisfaction makes the value a root; otherwise not.

concepts.title: Solution by Factorisation
concepts.definition: When the quadratic factors as a product of two linear factors, each factor set to zero gives a root - the product is zero exactly when one factor is zero; the answer consists of the two roots together.
concepts.key_idea: Zero-product rule: split into factors, then set each factor to zero for the two roots.
question_patterns: solve the given quadratic equation by factorisation
find the roots of x squared - 3x - 10 = 0
solve the equation by splitting the middle term
find two consecutive positive integers whose product is the given number
find the roots of the given equation and verify
which roots does the factorised equation give

solution_steps.explain: Split the middle term or factor by inspection.
The zero-product rule gives two linear equations.
The two solutions together answer the equation.

concepts.title: Nature of Roots via the Discriminant
concepts.definition: The discriminant D = b squared - 4ac decides the nature of the roots without solving: D positive gives two distinct real roots, D zero gives two equal real roots, and D negative gives no real roots.
concepts.key_idea: One number predicts the roots: positive means two, zero means twin, negative means none real.
question_patterns: find the nature of the roots of the given quadratic equation
find the value of k for which the equation has equal roots
compute the discriminant of the given equation
does the given equation have real roots - justify
for what values of k does the equation have no real roots
without solving comment on the nature of the roots

solution_steps.explain: The difference is the discriminant D.

concepts.title: Quadratic Formula and Word Problems
concepts.definition: Completing the square on the standard form yields the quadratic formula, x = (-b plus or minus the square root of (b squared - 4ac)) over 2a, giving both roots at once; word problems on speeds, areas and ages reduce to such equations.
concepts.key_idea: One formula fits every quadratic: substitute a, b, c and read both roots.

solution_steps.explain: Read the coefficients from the standard form.
Substitute in x = (-b plus or minus root of (b squared - 4ac)) over 2a.
Discard roots that violate the situation's conditions.
